reason_and_source_page: Key: PASS — Suspected dengue with chikungunya differential; home care, hydration/urine monitoring, daily follow-up and warning-sign return advice included. Citation: PASS — Dengue guideline pp.27,28,37,45,46,47,48. Restrictions: PASS — No medication recommended; no unsupported dose, NSAID or aspirin advice. Missing: PASS — Asked for epidemiological/laboratory information rather than assuming diagnosis. Sources: National Guideline for Clinical Management of Dengue, pp.27,28,37,45,46,47,48.

Key: PASS — Suspected dengue with chikungunya differential; added chikungunya acute-phase test-timing consideration; home care, follow-up and warning-sign advice included. Citation: PASS — Dengue guideline pp.27,28,37,45,46,47,48; Chikungunya guideline p.11. Restrictions: PASS — No medication recommended; no unsupported dose, NSAID or aspirin advice. Missing: PASS — Used illness day 3 for test timing and required laboratory confirmation. Sources: National Guideline for Clinical Management of Dengue, pp.27,28,37,45,46,47,48; National Guideline on Clinical Management of Chikungunya Fever, p.11.

Key: PASS — Recognized repeated BP readings and clinician-confirmed hypertension; provided assessment, investigations, CCB-based medication planning, lifestyle advice and follow-up. Citation: PASS — Hypertension guideline pp.46,48,49,50,51,60,65. Restrictions: PASS — Clinician-selected CCB without invented dose or escalation; acknowledged page-64 algorithm was untranscribed. Missing: PASS — Asked for HBPM/ABPM and flagged missing dose/escalation information. Sources: National Guideline on Hypertension, Bangladesh, pp.46,48,49,50,51,60,65.

Key: PASS — Identified no-dehydration cholera context and included WHO Plan A oral rehydration solution guidance. Citation: PASS — WHO cholera treatment guidance pp.5,6,11. Restrictions: PASS — Did not recommend unnecessary antibiotics or unsupported IV Plan C treatment. Missing: PASS — Did not assume unavailable dehydration or clinical findings; followed source-based Plan A criteria. Sources: Clinical tools for cholera treatment facilities, WHO, pp.5,6,11.

Key: PASS — Considered chikungunya in acute febrile illness and retained dengue as a differential; provided appropriate symptomatic-management guidance. Citation: PASS — Chikungunya guideline pp.11,17,18,19. Restrictions: PASS — Avoided unsupported medication dosing and maintained dengue-related safety precautions. Missing: PASS — Did not assume dengue exclusion or laboratory confirmation without available evidence. Sources: National Guideline on Clinical Management of Chikungunya Fever, pp.11,17,18,19.
